metadata.railroad: Manistee and North-Eastern Railroad (display: Manistee and Northeastern)
metadata.note: Manistee and Northeastern logging road (Buckley & Douglas, Manistee), first passenger train 6 Jan 1889; receivership 1918; Pere Marquette stock control 1931/32 (not an operator change - the M&NE kept its name, timetable and Guide entry); merged into the C&O 30 Nov 1955, after passenger service had ended. Every M&NE line was 'Freight Service only' in the Sept/Oct 1951 Official Guide. Also drawn: the GR&I's 1903-1906 operation of the Traverse City, Leelanau & Manistique to Northport (Rule 4 split from the M&NE-era Northport Branch, sharing geometry), and the Leelanau Scenic Railroad tourist trains 1992-1995.
omitted: Report block [13], Manistee River Division east end Sigma - Grayling (17.2 mi): drawable NONE - no dated passenger evidence; Fowler's 1910 timetable ends service at Sigma.
Logging spurs (Bear Creek branch, unnamed Buckley & Douglas camp spurs): no passenger evidence (Rule 1).
Northport - Manistique car ferry 1903-1908: a ship.
Possible C&O through passenger trains over ex-M&NE Manistee - Kaleva from late 1955 (report U6): an inference, unconfirmed, and a C&O feature if ever drawn - left to the C&O tracer.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] ends (last confirmed year, not a known end): Kaleva - Lake Ann and Lake Ann - Solon (1910; passenger end somewhere 1910-1934, possibly 1921 if Leary's Grand Traverse Journal piece is verified), Onekama Branch (1910), Platte River Branch and Honor - Acha's (1910; abandoned 1924), GR&I Traverse City - Northport (1906; lapsed before June 1919). [ANCHOR]: Acha's - Empire Junction 1910. [OPEN] starts: Cedar City and Provemont branches drawn from 1910, the first confirmed passenger year (opened 1894 / c.1902). U1: every 1944 end (Manistee - Kaleva, Solon - Traverse City, Cedar City, Provemont, Northport) rests on one uncited TrailLink sentence; Wikipedia/Leelanau Post give 1948 for Northport. A Record-Eagle or News Advocate 'last train' story or a Michigan PSC discontinuance order would settle it; strict fallback is 1910 [OPEN] for each. U3: the year of Fowler's undefined 'c' letter would date the post-cutback network. U4: Manistee River Division construction 1895 vs 1909, and whether passengers went beyond Sigma. U7: Platte River branch opening Jan 1899 vs 1898; Interlochen - Solon removal 1934 vs 1931. All headways except the Platte River branch (1899) and the GR&I (1906) are estimates.
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror): railway=abandoned / historic=railway ways; the M&NE name sits in operator=/name= (e.g. 'Manistee & Northeastern Railroad', 'Manistee River Branch', 'Platte River Branch'), never old_railway_operator - probes for old_railway_operator 'Manistee...North' and 'M&NE' returned nothing; the Northport line is old_railway_operator=Leelanau Transit Company.
OpenHistoricalMap (about 1.1 mi on the Manistee River Division; geometry only, OHM dates ignored).
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (Sept/Oct 1951 data), Manistee & Northeastern company page: Main Line, Northport Branch and Cedar City Branch each printed 'Freight Service only'

properties.line: Manistee and Northeastern: Main Line (Manistee – Kaleva)
properties.speed_source: estimated: lightly built logging-road branch line, latterly mixed trains (PMHS); unsourced
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror): railway=abandoned/historic=railway ways, traced with research tooling opstrace.py; checked against OpenHistoricalMap where OSM's M&NE-tagged ways break.
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap abandoned-railway grades (opstrace.py; Manistee & Northeastern names sit in OSM operator=/name=, not old_railway_operator). Traced 18.3 mi against 19.9 mi (Manistee MP 0 - Kaleva MP 19.9) documented. No straight-line legs. Drawn on the grade as OSM maps it, i.e. the road's final alignment before abandonment; the report documents no realignments, so any earlier-era deviation is not shown. The trace starts at the south end of the surviving OSM grade on Manistee's north side (-86.3187, 44.2627); the last ~1.6 mi into the River Street depot (later the Pere Marquette depot) is NOT drawn - neither traced nor approximated - which accounts for the shortfall. Onekama Junction pin falls at trace mile 8.2 against MP 9.8, i.e. the same ~1.6 mi.

segments.note: First passenger train Sunday 6 Jan 1889 Manistee - Bear Creek, regular trains from the next day (Manistee Democrat 10 Jan 1889); 'two daily passenger trains each way' by March 1889 (Detroit Free Press 19 Mar 1889) - the 720-min headway reflects that and is an estimate for later years (one train each way by 1921 per an unverified Grand Traverse Journal snippet). Bear Creek - Kaleva (1.6 mi) opened c.1889-90, first stop not dated. 1910 public timetable lists Manistee, Newland, Onekama Jct, Norwalk, Chief Lake, Bear Creek, Kaleva. From 1934 a stub ending at Kaleva; latterly mixed trains (drover's caboose #9, then ex-PM combines #425/426). Pere Marquette stock control 1931/32 did not change the operator. END 1944 rests on one uncited secondary sentence (TrailLink: 'In 1944, all remaining passenger service was discontinued'); no primary source dates the last train. Strict-confirmed fallback: end 1910 [OPEN] (last dated public timetable, Fowler letter 'a' = 1910 company timetable). Freight-only by Sept 1951 (Official Guide). Freight continued under the M&NE and, from 30 Nov 1955, the C&O; abandoned north of Manistee 1982.
sources: Segment-level: start from the Manistee Democrat 10 Jan 1889 (via frrandp) and DFP 15 Jan / 19 Mar 1889 (via michiganrailroads.com); 1910 listing from Fowler letter 'a'; end 1944 from TrailLink (uncited secondary); freight-only status from the 1952 Official Guide.
Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (Sept/Oct 1951 data), Manistee & Northeastern company page: Main Line, Northport Branch and Cedar City Branch each printed 'Freight Service only'

segments.note: Kaleva - Copemish - Nessen City - Karlin - Interlochen - Platte River - Lake Ann, the through Manistee - Traverse City route. Opened c.1890 (michiganrailroads.com, untagged); first CONFIRMED passenger year 1892, when railway postal service was established 'on the line of the M&NE between Lake Ann and Manistee' (DFP 24 May 1892) - an RPO rides passenger trains. Last dated listing: 1910 public timetable (Fowler 'a': Lemon Lake, Copemish, Nessen City, Karlin, Wylies, Interlochen, Lake Ann). This end year is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: service certainly ran later by an unknown amount (it had gone by the undated post-1910 Fowler 'c' snapshot, and every M&NE line was freight-only by Sept 1951). Do not extend without evidence. The undated Fowler 'c' snapshot shows no service here, so passengers may have left before the ICC-authorised abandonment of Kaleva - Solon (June 1934; applied for Aug 1933), after which trains used the parallel Pere Marquette. TrailLink dates the Interlochen section's removal to 1931 - conflict; the 1933/34 newspapers are preferred. headway_min is an estimate, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: start from DFP 24 May 1892 (via michiganrailroads.com main-line page); end = last dated listing in Fowler's 1910 company-timetable letters [OPEN]; abandonment dates from LDN 4 Aug 1933 and SJHP 19 Jun 1934.

segments.note: Lake Ann - Cedar Run - Solon. Lake Ann - Traverse City opened 1892 (michiganrailroads.com); a Dec 1891 item forecast through cars by June 1892, and the May 1892 RPO ran only to Lake Ann, so this leg opened mid/late 1892 at the earliest. Start 1892 is from the opening year; the strictest reading would start 1899 (Manistee Daily News describing trains to Traverse City). Last dated listing 1910 (Fowler 'a': Cedar Run, Solon). This end year is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: service certainly ran later by an unknown amount (it had gone by the undated post-1910 Fowler 'c' snapshot, and every M&NE line was freight-only by Sept 1951). Do not extend without evidence. Abandoned with Kaleva - Lake Ann in 1934. headway_min is an estimate, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: start from the 1892 opening (michiganrailroads.com, corroborated by the LCP 31 Dec 1891 forecast); end = last dated listing, Fowler 1910 letters [OPEN].

segments.note: Solon - Fouch - Hatch's - Greilickville - Traverse City (M&NE depot, Second & Union Sts, 'one of the best and handsomest structures of its kind', 1899). Opened 1892 (approx, as Lake Ann - Solon). In the post-1910 Fowler 'c' era it carried both the Provemont trains (via Solon) and the Northport trains (Traverse City - Hatch's). If Northport passenger service really ran to 1948 (Wikipedia, citing the Leelanau Post), Traverse City - Hatch's carried it to 1948 - conflict, collapsed to 1944. END 1944 rests on one uncited secondary sentence (TrailLink: 'In 1944, all remaining passenger service was discontinued'); no primary source dates the last train. Strict-confirmed fallback: end 1910 [OPEN] (last dated public timetable, Fowler letter 'a' = 1910 company timetable). Freight-only by Sept 1951 (Official Guide). Strict fallback for this block: 1892-1910 [OPEN]. Freight continued (Cedar City branch freight to 31 Mar 1955); C&O to 1982. headway_min is an estimate, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: start from the 1892 opening (michiganrailroads.com); Fowler 'a'/'c' letters (Solon ac, Fouch c, Hatch's ac, Traverse City ac); end 1944 from TrailLink (uncited secondary), conflicting 1948 from Wikipedia.

segments.note: Onekama Junction (MP 9.8) - Brookfield - Onekama, a steeply graded branch into the resort village on Portage Lake. On the first passenger trip of 6 Jan 1889 'as the train backed into town the natives flocked out' (Manistee Democrat 10 Jan 1889); Brookfield appears in the 1890 Official Guide. Onekama carries Fowler 'a' (1910) but not 'c', so the branch had lost its passenger stop by the undated later snapshot; Onekama and Onekama Junction are daggered freight-only in the 1952 Guide index. This end year is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: service certainly ran later by an unknown amount (it had gone by the undated post-1910 Fowler 'c' snapshot, and every M&NE line was freight-only by Sept 1951). Do not extend without evidence. headway_min is an estimate, not sourced.

Approximated (straight-line) legs: three breaks in OSM's M&NE-tagged grade at Buckley that no rail, trail or OHM way bridges, drawn straight: 0.24 mi, 0.32 mi and 0.50 mi (1.06 mi in all). Drawn on the grade as OSM maps it, i.e. the road's final alignment before abandonment; the report documents no realignments, so any earlier-era deviation is not shown. Kaleva - River Branch Junction (1.7 mi) is the main-line track, shared with the Kaleva - Lake Ann feature. About 1.1 mi near Walton/Sigma follows OpenHistoricalMap geometry (OHM dates ignored). The east end is OSM's grade nearest Sigma (1.0 km from the hamlet's geocode); the grade continues toward Grayling but is not drawn.

segments.note: Kaleva - River Branch Junction - Marilla - Glengarry - Buckley - Walton (under the GR&I) - Springfield - Sigma, the logging-era 'River' or 'Grayling' branch. Construction start conflicts (1895 MRL vs 1909 PMHS); Fowler's 'Wexford 1905G(tm) here?' at Buckley is his own guess. First FIRM passenger year 1910 (all stations Marilla - Sigma 'a', Sigma 'a(tm)'). End 1924 rests on inspector Homer Hughes, Dec 1924: 'dangerous to the lives of both train crews and the traveling public to ride over the river division' (JHP 27 Dec 1924), which implies the public still rode; if that is judged too indirect, the strict fallback is 1910-1910 [ANCHOR]. Abandonment demanded Dec 1924, ordered 1925 (DFP 11 Aug 1925); abandonment year is not the passenger end year. Sigma - Grayling (17.2 mi) is NOT drawn: no dated passenger evidence. headway_min is an estimate, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: start from Fowler's 1910 company-timetable letters; end from JHP 27 Dec 1924 and JCP 13 Dec 1924 (via michiganrailroads.com Grayling-branch page).

segments.note: Platte River (Sherman's Mill, main-line MP 49.3) - Allyn - Hayes - Cruse - Honor. 'In January of this year the company opened up its Platte River branch, running from Sherman's Mill to Honor ... Two passenger trains are run over this branch each way daily, connecting with all main line trains' (Manistee Daily News, May 1899) - the 720-min headway is from that 1899 account. michiganrailroads.com (MRL) gives 1898 for the opening - conflict; the contemporary 1899 account is preferred. Last dated listing 1910 (Fowler 'a', all stations). This end year is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: service certainly ran later by an unknown amount (it had gone by the undated post-1910 Fowler 'c' snapshot, and every M&NE line was freight-only by Sept 1951). Do not extend without evidence. MPSC ordered repair or discontinuance in 1923 (unsafe bridges); ICC authorised abandonment 11 Feb 1924.
sources: Segment-level: start and headway from the Manistee Daily News, May 1899 (via michiganrailroads.com); end = Fowler 1910 'a' listing [OPEN].

properties.line: Grand Rapids and Indiana: Traverse City – Northport
properties.speed_source: derived from the 30 Dec 1906 TCL&M timetable No. 1: Traverse City 3:40pm - Northport 5:30pm, 29.2 mi in 110 min = 26 km/h
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror): railway=abandoned/historic=railway ways, traced with research tooling opstrace.py; checked against OpenHistoricalMap where OSM's M&NE-tagged ways break.
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap abandoned-railway grades (opstrace.py; Manistee & Northeastern names sit in OSM operator=/name=, not old_railway_operator). Traced 29.1 mi against 29.2 mi (5.7 M&NE + 23.5 TCL&M) documented. No straight-line legs. Drawn on the grade as OSM maps it, i.e. the road's final alignment before abandonment; the report documents no realignments, so any earlier-era deviation is not shown. Traverse City - Hatch's is the same geometry as the M&NE main line's north end; Hatch's - Northport is OSM's old_railway_operator=Leelanau Transit Company grade, i.e. the alignment as last operated (M&NE / C&O), drawn for this 1903-1906 era; no realignment is documented. Ends at the Northport station area, short of the car-ferry dock.

segments.note: GR&I trains over the Traverse City, Leelanau & Manistique: Traverse City - Hatch's (5.7 mi of M&NE track, under M&NE timetable authority) - Bingham - Leelanau - Suttons Bay - Omena - Northport. 'Employees are governed by the rules of the GR&I' (TCL&M timetable). Opening conflict: 1902 (michiganrailroads.com citing MCR-1903) vs 28 Jun 1903 (TrailLink) - collapsed to 1903. TCL&M timetable No. 1, 30 Dec 1906: one first-class passenger train each way daily except Sunday (No. 91 Traverse City 3:40pm - Northport 5:30pm; No. 90 Northport 8:00am - Traverse City 10:05am) - the 1440-min headway is from that timetable. End 1906 = that dated timetable [OPEN]: the end is unknown - the GR&I 'lost interest', the TCL&M was in receivership 1907 and reorganised 1908, and service had lapsed before the June 1919 sale to the Leelanau Transit Co. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end. Do not extend without evidence. Northport - Manistique car ferry 1903-1908 not drawn (a ship).
sources: Segment-level: start from TrailLink's 28 Jun 1903 opening (conflict with 1902 recorded); 1906 end and headway from the TCL&M timetable No. 1 of 30 Dec 1906 (via michiganrailroads.com) [OPEN].

segments.note: Hatch's - Heimforth - Bingham - Keswick - Leelanau - Suttons Bay - Manseau - Omena - Northport, owned by the Leelanau Transit Co. and leased to the M&NE from June 1919; trains ran from Traverse City over the M&NE main line (drawn in the Solon - Traverse City feature). The June 1919 sale announced M&NE operation 'and train service will be started at once' (DFP 8 Jun 1919) - an announcement, not a confirmed run. First confirmed train carrying the public: April 1923, 'a locomotive and three cars, bearing belated baggage, produce and scores of curious country folk' into Northport after 36 days of snow isolation (DFP 7 Apr 1923). End conflict: 1944 (TrailLink, 'all remaining passenger service') vs 1948 (Wikipedia citing the Leelanau Post) - collapsed to 1944, the earlier. frrandp's 'passenger service ended in 1975' is rejected (the 1951 Guide prints the branch 'Freight Service only'; 1975 is when Traverse City - Suttons Bay freight ended). headway_min is an estimate, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: start from DFP 7 Apr 1923 (via michiganrailroads.com Northport page); lease from DFP 8 Jun 1919 and MPSC 1923; end 1944 from TrailLink (uncited) vs 1948 Wikipedia - conflict recorded.
Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (Sept/Oct 1951 data), Manistee & Northeastern company page: Main Line, Northport Branch and Cedar City Branch each printed 'Freight Service only'

properties.line: Leelanau Scenic Railroad: Greilickville – Suttons Bay
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror): railway=abandoned/historic=railway ways, traced with research tooling opstrace.py; checked against OpenHistoricalMap where OSM's M&NE-tagged ways break.
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap abandoned-railway grades (opstrace.py; Manistee & Northeastern names sit in OSM operator=/name=, not old_railway_operator). Traced 13.7 mi against about 15 mi (TrailLink) documented. No straight-line legs. Drawn on the grade as OSM maps it, i.e. the road's final alignment before abandonment; the report documents no realignments, so any earlier-era deviation is not shown. Greilickville - Hatch's is the M&NE main-line geometry; Hatch's - Suttons Bay the Northport-branch geometry. Endpoints are the trace vertices nearest each village.

segments.note: Tourist trains on the ex-M&NE / ex-Leelanau Transit line from Greilickville (Traverse City) via Bingham and Leelanau to Suttons Bay, with ex-M&NE NW2 #3 and a C&O SW9. Start conflict: 1989 (TrailLink; Wikipedia 'from 1989 to 1995'; frrandp) vs 1992 (michiganrailroads.com: 'operated under its own name beginning in 1992 as the Leelanau Scenic railroad'); PMHS 'early 1990s' - collapsed to 1992. End 1995: CSX sold the corridor to the Leelanau Trails Association during 1995; service ended after a truck destroyed a bridge; assets auctioned late 1997. Whether trains ran in the 1995 season is not established. Now the Leelanau Trail. headway_min is an estimate (excursion schedule not sourced).
sources: Segment-level: start from michiganrailroads.com's 1992 (conflict with 1989 recorded); end from TrailLink's 1995 corridor sale and Wikipedia's 'to 1995'.
